title: Learning to read: Mr. Robinson then Professor Foster
summary: He faked tunes by ear until about age seven or eight, when a clarinetist, Mr. Robinson, taught him to read and Foster took over and taught him until 'Bama State.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So, Mr. Foster was actually your first teacher?
Yes. I had, I had a teacher before that used to, I used to fake. You go, like you fake?

In other words, if I hear a tune on the radio before I learned to read, I could listen at that tune on the radio and go and pick up any instrument and play that tune without knowing how to read. So, when I got to a certain point, they said, they said well, we gonna learn you how to read. I must have been about, I guess I must have been about 7 or 8 years old. So, they took a big blackboard and put it in front of me and they made some notes, put a clef there, and then on. So, that's when I started to learn to read. Then, Professor Foster came in after that.

Drums and alto. I studied just a little instrument under him. But, Robinson came in very soon after that.
I mean, Foster came in very soon after that.

Robinson started. He started me to read.
